Also known as: Full-Time Equivalent; Full Time Equivalent
Definition: A way of counting staff that blends full-time and part-time hours into a single “equivalent number of full-time people” figure.
The number of people employed at a point in time, counting each person once whether they work full time or part time.

Also known as: Attrition
Definition: The share of employees who left over a period, voluntarily or otherwise.
How often employees are unexpectedly absent from scheduled work.
How long it takes, on average, to fill an open position from when it's posted.

Also known as: OT
Definition: Hours worked beyond an employee's standard schedule, usually paid at a higher rate.

Also known as: Direct Labor; DL
Definition: Staff whose work directly produces the product or service being sold (e.g. machine operators), as opposed to support roles.

Also known as: Indirect Labor; IDL
Definition: Staff who support production without directly making the product themselves -- maintenance, quality, supervision, and similar roles.
How long an employee has been with the company.

Also known as: Engagement Score
Definition: A measure of how motivated and committed employees feel, usually from survey results.

Also known as: Employee Net Promoter Score
Definition: How likely employees are to recommend the company as a place to work, on the same scale logic as customer NPS.

Also known as: HR Turnover Rate; Attrition Rate; Employee Turnover; Employee Turnover Rate; Staff Turnover
Definition: The share of employees who leave the organisation in a period, usually shown as a percentage of average headcount.

Also known as: Employee Retention; Employee Retention Rate
Definition: The share of employees who stay with the organisation over a period.

Also known as: Hires
Definition: The number of people who joined the organisation in a period.

Also known as: Vacancies; Open Roles
Definition: Jobs the organisation is trying to fill that are not yet filled.

Also known as: Training Completion
Definition: Time spent by employees on training, or the share of required training that has been completed.

Also known as: Absentee Rate
Definition: The share of scheduled working time lost to employee absence.

Also known as: Total Employees; Workforce
Definition: The number of people employed at a point in time.

Also known as: Cost of Turnover; Attrition Cost; Replacement Cost
Definition: The total cost of an employee leaving, including hiring a replacement, training and lost output while the role is empty.

Also known as: Voluntary Attrition; Resignation Rate; Voluntary Resignations
Definition: The share of employees who chose to leave, rather than being dismissed, in a period.

Also known as: Involuntary Attrition; Dismissal Rate; Terminations
Definition: The share of employees who left because the business ended their employment.

Also known as: Regretted Turnover; Regretted Loss; Regrettable Attrition
Definition: The share of leavers who the business would have preferred to keep, such as high performers.

Also known as: First Year Attrition; New Hire Turnover; 90-Day Attrition
Definition: The share of new joiners who leave within a short time, often the first year, after they started.

Also known as: Exits; Separations; Employees Left
Definition: The number of employees who left the business in a period.

Also known as: Starters; New Joiners; Employees Joined
Definition: The number of employees who joined the business in a period.

Also known as: Internal Transfers; Internal Moves; Internal Fill Rate
Definition: The share of roles that were filled by existing employees through moves or promotions.

Also known as: Promotions; Promotion Percentage
Definition: The share of employees who were promoted in a period.

Also known as: Management Span; Spans and Layers; Manager Span
Definition: The average number of people who report directly to each manager.

Also known as: Revenue per FTE; Sales per Employee
Definition: The total revenue divided by the number of employees, used as a broad measure of how productive the workforce is.

Also known as: Profit per FTE; Income per Employee
Definition: The total profit divided by the number of employees.

Also known as: Labor Cost Ratio; Payroll to Revenue; People Cost Ratio
Definition: The cost of employing people shown as a percentage of revenue.

Also known as: Payroll Cost; Salary Cost; Total Employee Cost; Staff Cost
Definition: The total money spent on pay, benefits and related costs for employees in a period.

Also known as: Average Pay; Mean Salary; Average Compensation
Definition: The average pay of employees, found by dividing total salary cost by the number of employees.

Also known as: Compa Ratio; Compensation Ratio
Definition: A person's pay divided by the middle of the pay range for their job. A figure of 1 means they are paid exactly at the midpoint.

Also known as: Pay Gap; Gender Pay Gap; Equal Pay
Definition: A comparison of pay between groups, such as men and women, doing similar work, used to check that pay is fair.

Also known as: Cost of Benefits; Benefits per Employee; Benefits Spend
Definition: The money spent on employee benefits such as health cover, pensions and allowances.

Also known as: Hiring Cost; Recruitment Cost; Cost of Hire
Definition: The total cost of recruiting, including adverts, agency fees and staff time, divided by the number of people hired.

Also known as: Time to Offer; Days to Hire; Recruitment Cycle Time
Definition: The number of days between a candidate applying, or a job being approved, and the offer being accepted.

Also known as: Offers Accepted; Job Offer Acceptance Rate
Definition: The share of job offers that the candidates accepted.

Also known as: Offers Declined; Offer Rejection Rate
Definition: The share of job offers that the candidates turned down.

Also known as: Applications per Role; Applicants per Job; Applicant Volume
Definition: The average number of people who applied for each open position.

Also known as: Hiring Source; Recruitment Channel; Candidate Source
Definition: The channel that the hired candidates came from, such as job boards, referrals or agencies.

Also known as: Referral Hires; Referral Hire Rate
Definition: The share of hires that came through a recommendation by an existing employee.

Also known as: Hire Quality; New Hire Performance
Definition: A score showing how well new hires perform and stay, often combining performance ratings and retention.

Also known as: Vacancy Percentage; Open Roles Rate
Definition: The share of all positions that are currently empty.

Also known as: Vacancy Age; Days Vacant; Time Vacant
Definition: The average number of days that a position stays empty.

Also known as: Hiring vs Plan; Hiring Target Achievement; Recruitment Plan Achievement
Definition: How many of the planned hires have been made, shown as a percentage of the hiring plan.

Also known as: Ramp-Up Time; Time to Proficiency
Definition: The time a new employee needs before working at a normal level.

Also known as: New Hire Retention Rate; First Year Retention
Definition: The share of new joiners who are still with the business after a set time, such as one year.

Also known as: Learning Spend per Employee; Training Spend per Head; L&D Spend
Definition: The money spent on training divided by the number of employees.

Also known as: Learning Effectiveness; Training ROI; Learning Impact
Definition: A measure of how far training led to better skills, behaviour or results after it was completed.

Also known as: Skills Gap; Skill Coverage; Competency Coverage
Definition: The share of the skills the business needs that its people already have.

Also known as: Succession Coverage; Bench Strength; Ready-Now Successors
Definition: The share of key roles that have at least one person ready, or nearly ready, to step into them.

Also known as: Appraisal Completion; Review Completion Rate; Performance Appraisals Done
Definition: The share of planned performance reviews that were completed on time.

Also known as: Rating Distribution; Performance Curve; Ratings Spread
Definition: The share of employees at each performance rating level, used to check that ratings are spread fairly.

Also known as: Top Talent Retention; Key Talent Retention
Definition: The share of the best performing employees who stayed with the business.

Also known as: Objectives Achieved; Goal Achievement; OKR Attainment
Definition: The share of employee or team goals that were reached in the period.

Also known as: Employee Satisfaction Score; ESAT; Job Satisfaction
Definition: A score from a survey showing how happy employees are with their work and workplace.

Also known as: Engagement Index; Engagement Survey Score
Definition: A score from a survey showing how committed and motivated employees are.

Also known as: Engagement Survey Response Rate; Survey Response Rate Employees
Definition: The share of employees who answered the staff survey.

Also known as: Recommend as a Place to Work; Employer Net Promoter
Definition: How likely employees are to recommend the business as a place to work.

Also known as: Sick Days; Sickness Absence; Days Absent
Definition: The total number of working days lost to absence in a period.

Also known as: Sickness Rate; Sick Leave Percentage; Sickness Absence Rate
Definition: The share of working days lost to sickness.

Also known as: Unscheduled Absence; Short-Term Absence; Casual Leave
Definition: Absence that was not arranged in advance, such as sickness or emergencies.

Also known as: Bradford Score; Absence Pattern Score
Definition: A score that gives extra weight to frequent short absences, as these are often more disruptive than a single long one.

Also known as: Leave Balance; Annual Leave Taken; Holiday Taken; Leave Liability
Definition: The share of annual leave that employees have taken, compared with what they are entitled to.

Also known as: Overtime Spend; Overtime Pay
Definition: The money paid for hours worked beyond normal hours.

Also known as: Extra Hours; Overtime Hours Worked
Definition: The total number of hours worked beyond normal working hours in a period.

Also known as: Contingent Workforce Ratio; Contractor Percentage; Temp Worker Share
Definition: The share of the workforce made up of contractors and temporary staff rather than permanent employees.

Also known as: Gender Ratio; Female Representation; Women in Workforce
Definition: The share of the workforce, or of a level such as management, that is made up of each gender.

Also known as: Diversity Ratio; Diversity and Inclusion; Diversity Index
Definition: A measure of how varied the workforce is in terms such as gender, age, background and ability.

Also known as: Average Age; Age Distribution; Workforce Age
Definition: The spread of employees across age groups, used to plan for retirements and recruitment.

Also known as: Grievance Rate; Employee Complaints; Employee Relations Cases
Definition: The number of formal complaints raised by employees in a period.

Also known as: Disciplinary Actions; Disciplinary Rate; Disciplinary Cases Opened
Definition: The number of formal disciplinary cases opened in a period.

Also known as: Wellbeing Index; Wellness Score; Employee Wellness
Definition: A score from a survey or health programme showing how well employees feel, in body and mind.

Also known as: Exit Survey Completion; Exit Interviews Held
Definition: The share of leavers who took part in an exit interview or survey.

Also known as: HR Headcount Ratio; HR Staff Ratio; Employees per HR
Definition: The number of employees served by each member of the HR team.

Also known as: HR Cost; HR Operating Cost; Cost of HR
Definition: The cost of running the HR function divided by the number of employees.
